# Authoring conventions for slides-builder decks

Reference document for the `slides-authoring` Claude Code skill and for
human authors editing reveal.js decks in this workspace. Installed into
`.claude/skills/slides-authoring/` by the `slides` binary, so the contract
described here always matches the binary that validates it.

---

## Folder layout and source-of-truth

```
decks/<name>/
  deck.html    ← source of truth; the only file you edit for content
  custom.css   ← per-deck CSS custom properties and theme overrides
  assets/
    vendor/    ← reveal.js + plugins + layout CSS; managed by the CLI
    fonts/     ← self-hosted fonts; never CDN links
    *.png …    ← deck-specific images and media
```

`deck.html` is a standard reveal.js HTML file with the reveal `Reveal.initialize()`
config inline. Both the editor and Claude Code read and write this file directly.
There is no sidecar JSON, no generated code, and no separate data model.

**A deck folder is fully self-contained.** Zip `decks/<name>/` and it renders
anywhere with zero network access.

---

## The layout vocabulary (`data-*` attributes)

Layout intent is declared as `data-*` attributes, not pixels and not utility
classes. A bundled stylesheet (`assets/vendor/slides-layout.css`) maps these
attributes to the corresponding flex/grid CSS at render time.

### WHY data-attributes instead of classes or inline styles

- The editor reads and writes clean key → value pairs with no class-string parsing.
- Reads almost like English to Claude Code and humans: "a row, gap 64, centered".
- Arbitrary integer values (gap 47) stay clean; Tailwind requires pre-generated
  utility classes and round-trips poorly.
- Alignment is expressed as *intent* (`data-align="center"`) rather than a pixel
  coordinate, so it survives resolution changes, aspect-ratio changes, and content
  edits automatically.

### The five primitives

| Primitive  | Declaration              | CSS result             |
|------------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| stack      | `data-lay="stack"`       | flex column            |
| row        | `data-lay="row"`         | flex row               |
| grid       | `data-lay="grid"`        | CSS grid               |
| layers     | `data-lay="layers"`      | z-stacked layers       |
| free       | `data-free` on element   | absolute + logical px  |

`data-free` is a boolean attribute (presence = active). It wins over `data-lay`
if both appear on the same element (the element is treated as free, not a container).

### Container attributes

These go on the element that bears `data-lay`:

| Attribute      | Applies to         | Allowed values                                              |
|----------------|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `data-lay`     | container (div…)   | `stack` \| `row` \| `grid` \| `layers`                     |
| `data-gap`     | any container      | non-negative integer (logical px)                           |
| `data-align`   | stack, row         | `start` \| `center` \| `end` \| `stretch`                  |
| `data-justify` | stack, row         | `start` \| `center` \| `end` \| `between` \| `around`      |
| `data-pad`     | any container      | non-negative integer (logical px)                           |
| `data-cols`    | grid               | integer count or CSS grid template string (e.g. `"1fr 2fr"`) |
| `data-rows`    | grid               | integer count or CSS grid template string                   |

### Child attributes

These go on an element that is a direct child of a container:

| Attribute    | Applies to      | Allowed values                            |
|--------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `data-grow`  | row/stack child | non-negative integer (flex-grow factor)   |
| `data-basis` | row/stack child | integer (logical px) or percentage string |
| `data-span`  | grid child      | positive integer >= 1 (column span)       |

### Free-element attributes

These go on any element that carries `data-free`. Coordinates use the 1920×1080
logical space (spec scaling-and-resolution: reveal.js scales this to any physical screen at present time).

| Attribute   | Values               |
|-------------|----------------------|
| `data-free` | boolean (presence)   |
| `data-x`    | logical px integer   |
| `data-y`    | logical px integer   |
| `data-w`    | logical px integer   |
| `data-h`    | logical px integer   |
| `data-rot`  | degrees integer      |

## `data-eid` — stable element IDs

Every element the editor manages carries `data-eid`: a stable, unique identifier
assigned on first edit and never changed afterwards.

### WHY `data-eid` is critical

The editor, Claude Code, and auto-animate all need to address individual elements
reliably across edit sessions. `data-eid` is the single identifier they share:

- Canvas selection state (the editor highlights the selected element).
- Claude Code targeting ("rewrite slide 4 body, eid `p1`").
- Auto-animate: `data-id` on animated elements is derived from `data-eid` so that
  pairs of slides can share a stable identity that reveal.js matches across the tween.
- "Highlight what Claude changed" feature in the editor status bar.

### Rules

1. **Unique per deck.** No two elements in `deck.html` share an eid.
2. **Stable.** Once assigned, never change. Renaming an eid breaks canvas selection
   and any Claude Code reference that mentioned it.
3. **Short and slug-like.** Convention: type-prefix + counter (`t1`, `p2`, `img3`,
   `row4`, `s5`). Match the prefix style used in the existing deck.
4. **On containers and leaves.** Assign `data-eid` to every `data-lay` container
   and every known leaf element (headings, `p`, `ul`, `ol`, `img`, `pre`, `code`,
   `table`, `figure`, `iframe`, `svg`, `video`, `audio`, and `div.math-block`).
5. **Not on passthrough elements.** Do not add `data-eid` to `script`, `style`,
   `meta`, `link`, `div` without `data-lay`, `span`, `em`, `strong`, `a`, `br`,
   `aside`, or any other element the editor does not manage.

## Slide-level attributes

These go on `<section>` elements:

| Attribute              | Values                                                        | Effect                                      |
|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `data-visibility`      | `hidden`                                                      | Hides the slide from the presentation       |
| `data-transition`      | `slide` \| `fade` \| `convex` \| `concave` \| `zoom` \| `none` | Per-slide transition override            |
| `data-transition-speed`| `default` \| `fast` \| `slow`                                | Per-slide transition speed                  |
| `data-auto-animate`    | boolean (presence)                                            | Enables auto-animate tween to/from adjacent |
| `data-theme` (P10)     | `black` \| `white` \| `league` \| `beige` \| `night` \| `moon` \| `solarized` \| `solarized-dark` \| `dracula` \| `sky` | Per-slide theme override |
| `data-layout` (P14)    | non-empty preset name (e.g. `title-body`, `two-column`)       | Layout-preset marker (drives "Change layout"); no reflow semantics |
| `data-footer-hidden` (P17) | boolean (presence)                                       | Opts this slide out of the deck-level footer overlay |
| `data-background-color` | any CSS color                                                | reveal.js per-slide background color        |
| `data-background-gradient` | CSS gradient string                                       | reveal.js per-slide background gradient     |
| `data-background-image` (P16) | `assets/…` relative path (offline-first)               | reveal.js per-slide background image        |
| `data-background-video` (P16) | `assets/…` relative path (offline-first)               | reveal.js per-slide background video        |
| `data-background-size` / `-position` / `-repeat` / `-opacity` / `-video-loop` / `-video-muted` | CSS / reveal pass-through strings | Background tuning (tolerated verbatim) |

Nested `<section>` elements create reveal's 2D slide grid (vertical stacks).

### Child-container and leaf markers (P14 / P17)

- `data-slot="<role>"` — on a child container of a preset layout (e.g. `content`,
  `sidebar`). Non-empty string; informational only (no reflow semantics).
- `data-chart` + `data-chart-data` — on a `<canvas>` leaf: the chart type string
  plus a parseable Chart.js JSON config `{type, data, options?}`. A bare
  `<canvas>` without `data-chart` stays passthrough.
- `data-qr` (+ `data-qr-*`) — on a `<div>` leaf: a QR code. `data-qr` is the
  encoded payload (a URL or text; non-empty). The div is **empty on disk** — the
  vendored QR plugin renders an inline SVG into it at runtime (offline; renders in
  editor / present / PDF, a static placeholder in the navigator thumbnail). A bare
  `<div>` without `data-qr` stays passthrough. Encoding options (all optional):
  - `data-qr-ec="L|M|Q|H"` — error-correction level (default `M`).
  - `data-qr-fg` / `data-qr-bg` — module / background colours (default
    `#000000` / `#ffffff`). These are **functional inputs to generation**, stored
    as attributes (not CSS) so the renderer can draw scannable modules — keep
    strong contrast or the code won't scan.
  - `data-qr-quiet` — quiet-zone width in modules, non-negative int (default `4`).
  - also carry an `aria-label` (e.g. `QR code: <payload>`) so the code is
    described to assistive tech.

  A QR is a fixed-size graphic you position on the slide, so the editor inserts it
  as a **free** block (`data-free` + `data-x/y/w/h`, sized by the free-layout CSS)
  — draggable/resizable on the canvas. Hand-authoring, either make it free or place
  it inside a layout slot; a bare `<div data-qr>` dropped straight under a
  `data-layout` section overflows off the slide edge.

  Example: `<div data-qr="https://example.com" data-qr-ec="M" data-qr-fg="#000000"
  data-qr-bg="#ffffff" data-qr-quiet="4" aria-label="QR code: https://example.com"
  data-free data-x="820" data-y="400" data-w="280" data-h="280"></div>`

### Inline marks (rich text within a leaf, P17)

Inside a text leaf the editor recognises an allowlist of inline marks —
`strong` · `em` · `u` · `s` · `a[href,target,rel]` · `span[style: color, font-size]`
(plus `br`). Legacy tags are normalised (`b`→`strong`, `i`→`em`, `font`→`span`);
disallowed tags/attributes are unwrapped or stripped on save; `javascript:` /
`vbscript:` / `data:` anchor hrefs are neutralised. Inline marks carry **no**
`data-eid` — they are addressed by the leaf's `data-eid` plus a selection range.
Unlike resource `src`s, external `<a href>` link targets are not flagged by the
offline guard (they are navigation, not loaded assets).

## Idempotent round-trip (byte-stable parse/serialize)

> `parse → model → serialize` produces **no diff** when no edits are made.

This is a tested invariant. It matters because:

- Without it, the editor and Claude Code would churn each other's files on every
  save/reload, polluting git history with noise diffs.
- It enables "highlight what Claude changed" to work accurately (diff the previous
  bytes against the new bytes).

**Consequences for authors:**

- Attribute order in generated HTML is deterministic and must not be reordered
  by hand tools (prettier, etc.) that the editor will then "undo" on next save.
- Whitespace inside elements managed by the editor follows the formatter's rules.
  Do not add extra blank lines or indentation inside managed elements.
- Passthrough elements are always written back byte-for-byte: their formatting
  is whatever you originally wrote.

---

## Never destroy the unknown (passthrough rule)

HTML the editor cannot fully represent is **preserved verbatim**. The editor
recognises elements by tag name and `data-*` attributes. Anything else is
classified as `passthrough` and written back byte-identical.

This means:

- Reveal.js plugins, custom widgets, embedded iframes, raw SVG, `<script>`,
  `<style>`, `<aside class="notes">`, metadata — all survive every edit cycle.
- Claude Code can write arbitrary reveal.js constructs between sessions; they
  will not be lost on next save.
- The editor marks passthrough slides/elements with a "source only" badge so
  the author knows they cannot be visually edited on the canvas.

---

## Offline-first (never CDN URLs)

> Core editing, presenting, and PDF export work with zero network access.

reveal.js, highlight.js, KaTeX, themes, and fonts are all vendored locally into
`assets/vendor/`. The deck template references them with relative paths.

**Rules:**

1. Never reference `https://` URLs in `<img>`, `<link>`, `<script>`, `url()`,
   or `@import` inside `deck.html` or `custom.css`.
2. All images, video, and media: copy into `assets/` before referencing.
3. Fonts: download once and place in `assets/fonts/`. Use `@font-face` in
   `custom.css` with a relative path.
4. Do not modify files under `assets/vendor/`. Use `slides vendor <name>` to
   refresh them after a binary upgrade.

The only intentionally network-dependent features are image-acquisition helpers
(Unsplash, Giphy, Gemini). These always localize what they fetch into `assets/`
before referencing the local copy in `deck.html`. They degrade gracefully
(with UI feedback) when offline.

---

## Ownership split

> The editor owns **layout** (`data-*`). The author/Claude owns **styling**
> (Tailwind utility classes / inline `style=""` / `custom.css`).

The editor never reads or rewrites class strings or inline styles for layout
purposes; it only reads/writes `data-*` attributes. This means:

- You can add any Tailwind utility class, inline style, or CSS variable.
- These pass through every editor save/reload cycle untouched.
- The editor's layout engine ignores them.

---

## Versioning and secrets

- **Git is the durable revision history.** A deck folder (`deck.html` + `custom.css`
  + `assets/`) is git-friendly: one directory, human-readable HTML, binary assets.
  The in-editor undo stack is session-only.
- **API keys** (Unsplash, Giphy, Gemini) come from env vars or a gitignored local
  config file. Never commit them in `config.toml` or anywhere else in the repo.

---

## CLI reference

```bash
slides [serve]        # start the editor on port 3000 (default action)
slides new <name>     # scaffold decks/<name>/ with template + vendored reveal.js
slides vendor <name>  # (re)vendor reveal.js into an existing deck after binary upgrade
```

```bash
slides add-slide <name>   # append a starter <section> to the deck (byte-stable)
slides validate <name>    # check well-formedness: valid data-*, unique eids, assets exist
```

Run `slides validate` after every Claude Code edit. It exits non-zero with
readable diagnostics on the offending line/eid, catching invalid enum values,
duplicate eids, missing or external assets, and parse errors before they
silently break the canvas or presenter. The editor enforces the same rules over
HTTP (`POST /api/decks/{name}/validate`) and gates its own save path on them.

## Attribute cross-reference (implementation source)

The canonical attribute names and allowed-value sets are defined in the
**slides-builder source tree** (not in this workspace — a decks workspace is
usually a separate repo, and these paths are here to say where the contract is
maintained, not to be opened from here):

- `web/src/lib/model/layout.ts` — `LayValue`, `AlignValue`, `JustifyValue`, `LayoutProps`; chart, QR, and preset/slot accessors
- `web/src/lib/model/theme.ts` — `THEME_NAMES` and the `data-background-*` set
- `web/src/lib/model/inline.ts` — `INLINE_MARK_TAGS` and the inline-mark allowlist/normalisation
- `web/src/lib/model/classify.ts` — element classification rules (container / leaf / free / passthrough)
- `internal/validate/validate.go` — the Go re-implementation of the same allowed-sets (keep in sync)
- `internal/deck/deck.go` — deck template, vendored asset structure, CLI commands
- `specs/layout-vocabulary.md` — design intent and contract
- `specs/principles-and-invariants.md` — offline-first, round-trip, never-destroy
- `internal/skill/assets/slides-authoring/` — the source of truth for this document
  and `SKILL.md`; the binary embeds them and installs a copy into each workspace
